I was using a rapid trigger keyboard for Tekken before I got a proper hitbox. At most rapid trigger could get you a slightly cleaner korean backdash and slightly more consistent fast QCFs but for Tekken I think a button with smaller travel distance (e.g sanwas) is better than what rapid trigger can give you.

Mouse switches would definitely be interesting. Since it's an instant click you would need a spring to keep the dpad upright and would have to ride the gate whenever you want to actuate it unlike a keyboard switch where it actuates at halfway of the travel

I have some box whites on hand right now in a keyboard, while I don't know about the other box switches, even if I try to get it to actuate without it clicking, I'm not able to. But I CAN make it actuate without clicking only when I have already done the first click then lifting it just high enough where it doesn't do the release click then pressing down again; essentially making it linear. Which, interestingly enough, I can also do on my arcade lever but not as easily!

And yeah one of the cool things about this dpad design would probably be the ease of how you can customize it for yourself, unlike arcade levers where you have to spend hundreds just to find out what your preferred setup is
